description: The world's most significant rivers and lakes with geographic and cultural context

nile.significance: Longest river in world (debated with Amazon); civilization of ancient Egypt; flows north

amazon.significance: Largest by volume (20% of global river discharge); world's largest rainforest basin

yangtze.significance: Longest river in Asia; Three Gorges Dam (largest hydroelectric plant)

mississippi_missouri.significance: Largest North American river system; drains 40% of continental USA

volga.significance: Longest river in Europe; flows into Caspian Sea; crucial to Russian history

rhine.significance: Economic backbone of Western Europe; major industrial waterway

danube.significance: Flows through 10 countries; historically important trade route

ganges.significance: Sacred river of Hinduism; supports 500+ million people

congo.significance: Second largest by volume; deepest river in world (220m); Congo rainforest

caspian_sea.significance: World's largest lake; technically an inland sea; borders 5 countries

superior.significance: Largest freshwater lake by area; part of Great Lakes system

victoria.significance: Largest lake in Africa; shared by Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania; source of White Nile

michigan.significance: Only Great Lake entirely within USA

baikal.significance: World's deepest lake; contains 20% of world's unfrozen surface fresh water; oldest lake

dead_sea.significance: Saltiest water body (10× saltier than ocean); lowest point on Earth's surface

titicaca.significance: Highest navigable lake in world; Peru-Bolivia border; ancient Inca significance

great_lakes_system.significance: 21% of world's surface fresh water; shared USA-Canada; St. Lawrence Seaway
